data.title: To be a better programmer, write little proofs in your head
data.author: mprast
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种帮助更快、更准确编写代码的技巧，即在编写代码时，在脑海中构建一个证明，确保代码能实现预期功能。这种“在线”推理需要大量练习，但熟练后，代码通常能在第一或第二次尝试时正常工作。文章还讨论了单调性概念在代码中的应用，例如通过检查点机制确保代码只能向前推进。此外，文章提到不可变性，通过创建不可变对象避免对象在使用过程中被修改。最后，文章介绍了前置条件和后置条件的概念，用于定义函数运行前后的状态，以帮助验证函数实现是否正确。这些技巧有助于简化代码推理过程，提高开发效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过编写小证明或使用形式化方法（如不变量和前置/后置条件）来确保代码正确性的方法和实践

不同观点：
• pclowes 支持使用测试驱动开发（TDD）作为确保代码正确性的有效方法。强调编写简单测试、观察测试失败、然后编写最少代码以通过测试的纪律性，并指出测试的耦合度和可维护性是提升设计信心的关键。
• hiAndrewQuinn 通过二分查找的例子说明不变量和前置/后置条件在算法中的重要性，引用Jon Bentley的实验表明即使是专业程序员也常在实现简单算法时出错。
• JohnMakin 分享了自己在数学考试中通过提前思考清楚再下笔的方法，并将其类比为编写代码前的清晰构思，认为这种方法有助于减少错误。
• ge96 认为虽然不具备高学历或算法能力，但通过实际项目和经验仍能成为优秀开发者，强调实用技能和代码简化。
• bluetomcat 认为在全新项目中编写易于验证的代码是可行的，但在跨单元调用和涉及全局状态时难度增加。
• gregorygoc 认为编写正确证明和程序验证很困难，主张简化、清晰和通用性的编程原则，并指出竞争性编程有助于学习正确技术。
• thesuperbigfrog 提倡在代码中使用设计契约（Design-by-Contract）来明确前置、后置条件和不变量，列举了支持该方法的编程语言和库。
• xg15 补充了不可变性和多线程环境下的代码简化优势。
• GMoromisato 分享了具体案例分析对解决bug的帮助，强调从具体案例中学习。
• nayuki 强调了循环不变量和结构归纳在计算机科学证明中的重要性，提供了相关资源。
• bubblebeard 认为在非工作状态下（如散步或做家务时）思考问题更有效。
• tristramb 回顾了T. J. Dekker和Edgser Dijkstra在程序设计中引入数学证明思想的历史背景。
• pokemyiout 提出了对文章中归纳部分的疑问，质疑函数命名的准确性。
• taeric 认为这种方法借鉴了数学中的公理和定理体系，强调在系统知识的不同方面建立独立词汇，同时指出数据一致性问题的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于编写代码前进行详细思考和形式化证明的实际可行性，特别是在复杂项目或跨单元调用时。
• 不同的方法（如TDD、设计契约、数学证明思想）在不同场景下的有效性和适用性被广泛讨论。
• 实际案例和经验分享（如GMoromisato的bug修复过程）提供了具体实践中的见解和学习机会。

44573409.article_content:
This is a brief write-up of a trick I learned that helps me write code faster and more accurately. I say "trick", but it's really something I started to do without noticing  as I moved further into my career.
When you're working on something difficult, sketch a proof in your head as you go that your code will actually do what you want it to do. A simple idea, but easier said than done: doing this "online" without interrupting your flow takes a lot of practice. But once you get really good at it, you'll find that a surprising amount of the time your code will work on the first or  second try. It feels a little magical.
There are lots of ways to pull this off, and I don't want to be too prescriptive. I'll just list a few examples of the kinds of things I find myself reasoning about on the fly, so you get the general idea.
Monotonicity
Something to keep an eye out for when proving things to yourself about your code is which parts are
monotonic
.
You're probably familiar with monotonic functions from mathematics. Informally, they're functions that don't "go backwards" - i.e. an increasing monotonic function can only increase or stay the same, while a decreasing monotonic function can only decrease or stay the same (these are also known as
nondecreasing
and
nonincreasing
functions, respectively.)
The concept of monotonic
code
is a little more nebulous than the concept of a monotonic function, but it captures the same idea of a process that can only proceed in one direction. Check-pointing, for example, is a great example of monotonicity. If you have (say) a script that needs to perform multiple tasks in sequence, you can keep a bit of state around on disk that details how many tasks you have completed so far. If something goes wrong and your script crashes, it can check the on-disk state to figure out how far it got, then start again from the earliest state that hasn't been run yet.
Checkpointing means that the "current step" pointer in your script can only go forwards, since the script can't regress and re-run a step it's already done. In this sense the script progresses
monotonically
, and it's apparent that if the script ever completes successfully, it will have run every step exactly once.
Keeping this kind of activity log is a simple idea that often pops up in surprising places, such as journaling file systems and database write-ahead logs. Another, more involved database example is an LSM tree. LSM trees are used in some databases to store rows in-memory and on-disk, and most of the time they are purely additive. Put loosely - an LSM tree keeps a log of all inserts, deletes, and updates, and scans the log to reconstruct the appropriate value of the row when the row is read. Stale operations are periodically discarded to save space in a process called compaction. The space taken by an LSM tree
only
grows (except during compaction, when it
only
shrinks.)
You can compare this to a B-tree, which is a more traditional database structure that deletes and updates rows in place. B-trees generally have to do a lot more work to reclaim the freed space after a delete, restructure things so there's room if an update grows a row, make sure there's enough buffer, etc. If you want, read a little bit more about B-trees and LSM trees, and see which one feels more intuitive to reason about.
It's worth keeping an eye out for monotonicity, because you can usually use it to rule out wide swaths of possible outcomes. Another variation on this theme is immutability (which in a lot of ways is monotonicity's cousin) - when you create an immutable object, that object cannot be modified. Values can be assigned to an immutable object exactly once, at the time of the object's construction; you can't "back out" or "undo" the assignments. This allows you to ignore, out of hand, all scenarios in which an object might change out from under your feet.
Pre- and post-conditions
Pre-conditions and post-conditions are ways to specify constraints on the behavior of a function. A function's
pre-conditions
are the things that are assumed to be true just before the function runs. These can be conditions on the function's input, or more general claims about the program's state or environment. A function's
post-conditions
are things that are assumed to be true just after the function returns. As with pre-conditions, these claims can involve just about anything. If the pre-conditions of a function are true before the function runs, and the post-conditions are
not
true after the function finishes, then the function is not implemented correctly, at least according to the specified constraints.
These are simple (even obvious) concepts and not really proof techniques in and of themselves, but simply keeping track of what they are in formal terms can aid your reasoning.
(Sometimes you may come to find that your function does not have well-defined pre- and post-conditions, which is also good to know!)

data.article_summary: 美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）的研究人员开发出世界上最精确的原子钟，能够将时间测量到小数点后19位。这一“量子逻辑钟”依靠量子计算技术，将带电的铝离子与镁离子配对，经过20年的持续改进，其精度比之前的记录高出41%，稳定性是其他离子钟的2.6倍。该钟的精度和稳定性得益于对每个组件的精心改进，包括激光、离子阱和真空室。铝离子钟的“滴答”频率极其稳定，受环境条件影响小，但由于铝离子难以用激光探测和冷却，研究团队通过镁离子辅助冷却和读数，实现了精确测量。该成果发表在《物理评论快报》上，有助于重新定义秒并推动科学和技术进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高精度原子钟的技术进展及其应用和意义

不同观点：
• **技术细节和精度讨论**：
   - mikewarot提到现代原子钟的精度，即使是几厘米的高度变化也能通过重力/时间膨胀效应测量出来。他还提到个人可以购买精度略低的铯原子钟。
   - perihelions提供了相关预印本链接，讨论了单离子钟的系统不确定性达到 $5.5\times10^{-19}$。
   - jasonthorsness指出铝离子钟比铯钟更精确但更难使用，目前技术进步解决了其应用难题。
   - gwerbret强调文章中提到的“精度”应与“准确性”区分，指出文章用词不当。

• **应用和实际问题**：
   - Babkock质疑如何测量时钟的准确性，如果所有时钟都有一点误差怎么办。
   - mlhpdx提出问题，讨论这种“时钟”是否更像是一种“时钟信号”，类似于位置编码器的相对和绝对性质。
   - duncangh幽默地提到在停电后重新设置家用电器的时间与这种高精度时钟对齐的困难。

• **政策和资金讨论**：
   - frankfrank13提到NOAA和NIST的相关性，并担心该校区的未来风险。
   - tguvot指出访问NIST的NTP服务器需要通过传统邮寄或传真方式获取密钥，这一过程可能因办公限制而延迟。
   - searine强调这是由美国税收资助的基础科学研究，呼吁不要挪用科学创新的未来资金。

• **国际竞争和技术风险**：
   - throw0101c认为尽管技术进步显著，但美国（及西方）在分发和弹性方面似乎落后。他提到中国通过北斗卫星、eLoran和光纤网络在时间同步方面取得进展，并指出GPS/GNSS存在重大风险，已成为单一故障点。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：
   - 技术精度与实际应用之间的差距。有人对如何在日常设备中应用这种高精度技术表示怀疑。
   - 关于科学创新资金使用的讨论，反映了科研进步与政策支持之间的依赖关系。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：
   - 对NIST相关技术和项目的具体操作细节的讨论，如访问NTP服务器的程序问题。
   - 对新技术突破的兴奋与幽默反应，如kridsdale3和riwsky的简短评论，表现出对科学进步的赞赏。

NEWS
NIST Ion Clock Sets New Record for Most Accurate Clock in the World
July 14, 2025
Share
Facebook
Linkedin
X.com
Email
NIST researchers have made the most accurate atomic clock to date — one that can measure time down to the 19th decimal place.
This “quantum logic clock,” under continuous development for 20 years, relies on quantum computing techniques that pair an electrically charged aluminum atom (ion) with a magnesium ion.
This new result contributes to the international effort to define the second with a much greater level of accuracy than before, enabling new scientific and technological advances.
(From left to right) Mason Marshall, David Hume, Willa Arthur-Dworschack and Daniel Rodriguez Castillo stand in front of the aluminum ion clock at NIST. With its recent improvements, the clock can pave the way for the campaign to redefine the second as well as explore new ideas in physics.
Credit:
R. Jacobson/NIST
There’s a new record holder for the most accurate clock in the world. Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have improved their
atomic clock
based on a trapped aluminum ion. Part of the latest wave of
optical atomic clocks
, it can perform timekeeping with 19 decimal places of accuracy.
Optical clocks are typically evaluated on two levels — accuracy (how close a clock comes to measuring the ideal “true” time, also known as systematic uncertainty) and stability (how efficiently a clock can measure time, related to statistical uncertainty). This new record in accuracy comes out of 20 years of continuous improvement of the aluminum ion clock. Beyond its world-best accuracy, 41% greater than the previous record, this new clock is also 2.6 times more stable than any other ion clock. Reaching these levels has meant carefully improving every aspect of the clock, from the laser to the trap and the vacuum chamber.
The team published its results in
Physical Review Letters
.
“It’s exciting to work on the most accurate clock ever,” said Mason Marshall, NIST researcher and first author on the paper. “At NIST we get to carry out these long-term plans in precision measurement that can push the field of physics and our understanding of the world around us.”
NIST physicist David Hume holds the newly modified ion trap for the aluminum ion clock. By modifying the trap, the aluminum ion and its magnesium ion partner were able to “tick” unperturbed.
Credit:
R. Jacobson/NIST
The aluminum ion makes an exceptionally good clock, with an extremely steady, high-frequency “ticking” rate. Its ticks are more stable than those of cesium, which provides the
current scientific definition
of the second, said David Hume, the NIST physicist leading the aluminum ion clock project. And the aluminum ion isn’t as sensitive to some environmental conditions, like temperature and magnetic fields.
But the aluminum ion is kind of shy, Marshall explained. Aluminum is difficult to probe and cool with lasers, both necessary techniques for atomic clocks. The research group therefore paired the aluminum ion with magnesium. Magnesium doesn’t have the beautiful ticking properties of aluminum, but it can be easily controlled with lasers. “This ‘buddy system’ for ions is called quantum logic spectroscopy,” said Willa Arthur-Dworschack, a graduate student on the project. The magnesium ion cools the aluminum ion, slowing it down. It also moves in tandem with its aluminum partner, and the state of the clock can be read out via the magnesium ion’s motion, making this a “quantum logic” clock. Even with this coordination, there was still an array of physical effects to characterize, said Daniel Rodriguez Castillo, also a graduate student on the project.
“It’s a big, complex challenge, because every part of the clock’s design affects the clock,” Rodriguez Castillo said.
One challenge was the design of the trap where the ions are held, which was causing tiny movements of the ions, called excess micromotion, that were lowering the clock’s accuracy. That excess micromotion throws off the ions’ tick rate. Electrical imbalances at opposite sides of the trap were creating extra fields that disturbed the ions. The team redesigned the trap, putting it on a thicker diamond wafer and modifying the gold coatings on the electrodes to fix the imbalance of the electric field. They also made the gold coatings thicker to reduce resistance. Refining the trap this way slowed the ions’ motion and let them “tick” unperturbed.

data.title: Show HN: Shoggoth Mini – A soft tentacle robot powered by GPT-4o and RL
data.author: cataPhil
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者在探索机器人表现力和互动性方面的实验过程，特别是通过构建名为Shoggoth Mini的软体机器人。最初，作者受到Apple的ELEGNT论文和SpiRobs的启发，开始研究如何让机器人更具表现力。在硬件设计中，作者意外地通过使用不同颜色的3D打印材料和简单的绘画面部特征，创造了一个既可爱又略带诡异的机器人外观。在解决了一系列技术问题后，如电缆缠绕和校准，作者成功设计出一个可以通过触控板直观控制的机器人 tentacle。该系统的控制分为低层级的开环和闭环策略，并通过简单的2D到3D映射实现自动控制。最终，Shoggoth Mini成为了一个探索机器人表现力的实验平台，展示了如何通过意外发现和迭代改进设计出更自然的机器人互动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能与机器人技术的发展及其与人类心理的交互

不同观点：
• **关于机器人是否应具有“生命感”的讨论**：
   - **rainingmonkey** 认为，虽然机器人具有表现力，但随着人类对其工作原理的熟悉，机器人会失去“生命感”。他提出一个问题：我们是否真的需要让机器人感觉像是活着的？或者在某个超过表现力的点上，系统会因为过于不可预测而让人类感到不适。
   - **huevosabio** 支持为非人类实体添加表现力，认为这是很酷的想法，显示出对机器人表达能力的兴趣。
   - **zhyder** 则明确表示不希望机器人看起来像自然生物，担心未来无法区分自然和机器人，强调了保持机器人外观明显机械化的重要性。

• **对技术实现及其实际应用的讨论**：
   - **dylan604** 提到GPT处理延迟带来的不适感，并建议通过增加LED指示灯等方式改善用户体验。他还对GPT-4o持续监听音频流的功能表示担忧。
   - **typs** 认为目前机器人技术过于集中在人形机器人上，而更期待像蜘蛛/鱿鱼混合型的机器人，反映出对多样化机器人形态的期望。
   - **dunefox** 则关注模型的大小问题，提出是否可以使用更小的模型来实现相同功能。

• **对机器人形态和文化联想的讨论**：
   - **sparrish** 明确表示不希望类似“异形抱脸虫”的机器人出现在自己桌上，反映出对某些机器人形态的反感。
   - **ge96** 和 **KaoruAoiShiho** 则联想到了电影和漫画中的角色（如“章鱼博士”和“蜘蛛侠”），显示出对机器人形态的文化联想。
   - **dvngnt_** 通过日本媒体联想到某种未来的发展方向，虽然没有具体说明，但显示出对文化背景影响的关注。

补充讨论：
• **关于机器人技术的实际应用和研究**：
   - **SequoiaHope** 分享了对“连续体机器人”（continuum robots）的研究，并提供了一个讲座链接，强调了这种机器人在医学领域的应用潜力。
   - **regularfry** 提到了一篇关于“SpiRobs”机制的论文，并指出其专利申请的动向，显示出对技术专利和实际应用的关注。

• **关于未来技术普及的担忧**：
   - **micromacrofoot** 幽默地提到未来LLM（大型语言模型）可能会像WiFi和触屏一样普及，甚至让冰箱“哭泣”，反映出对技术过度普及和拟人化的担忧。

争议焦点：
• **机器人是否应该具有“生命感”以及其形态和行为的不可预测性**：一方认为机器人需要具有某种不可预测性和生命感，另一方则担心这种不可预测性会让人类感到不适，且有人明确反对机器人过于拟人化或模仿自然生物。

44572377.article_content:
Over the past year, robotics has been catching up with the LLM era. Pi’s π0.5
can clean unseen homes
. Tesla’s Optimus can follow
natural language cooking instructions
. These systems are extremely impressive, but they feel stuck in a utilitarian mindset of robotic appliances. For these future robots to live with us, they must be expressive. Expressiveness communicates internal state such as intent, attention, and confidence. Beyond its functional utility as a communication channel, expressiveness makes interactions feel natural. Without it, you get the textbook
uncanny valley
effect.
Earlier this year, I came across Apple’s
ELEGNT
paper, which frames this idea rigorously through a Pixar-like lamp to show how posture and timing alone can convey intention. Around the same time, I discovered
SpiRobs
, a soft tentacle robot that feels oddly alive with just simple movements. One system was carefully designed to express intent while the other just moved, yet somehow felt like it had intent. That difference was interesting. I started building Shoggoth Mini as a way to explore it more directly. Not with a clear goal, but to see what would happen if I pushed embodiment into stranger territory. This post retraces that process, the happy accidents, and what I learned about building robots.
ELEGNT
SpiRobs
SpiRobs demo
Hardware
The first challenge was creating a testbed to explore the control of SpiRobs. I started very simple: a plate to hold three motors, and a dome to lift the tentacle above them. This setup wasn’t meant to be the final design, only a platform for quick experimentation. However, halfway through 3D printing, I ran out of black filament and had to finish the dome in grey. This made it look like the dome had a mouth. When my flatmate saw it sitting on my desk, he grabbed a marker and drew some eyes. It looked good: cute, weird, slightly unsettling. I used ChatGPT to explore renders, and decided that this accident would become the form factor.
Later, I mounted stereo cameras on the dome to track the tentacle. Robot eyes are eerie. You keep expecting movement, but nothing ever happens. That prediction error
focuses attention even more
.
The original open-spool design relied on constant cable tension, but any slight perturbation (such as testing a buggy new policy) would make the cables leave the spool and tangle around the motor shafts. The process to fix it required untying the knot at the tip holding the cables together, and dismantling the whole robot. Adding simple spool covers eliminated most tangles and made iteration dramatically faster.
Another key step was adding a calibration script and pre-rolling extra wire length. This made it possible to:
Unroll and reroll the cables to open the robot without having to untie the tip knot, speeding up iteration dramatically
Calibrate cable tension precisely and as often as needed
Give control policies slack to work with during motion
Rolling the cables back after working on Shoggoth Mini's insides
Finally, as you can see in the video, the standard 3-cable SpiRobs design sags under its own weight. This makes consistent behavior hard to reproduce. I had to thicken the spine just enough to prevent sag, but not so much that it would deform permanently under high load.
You can explore the current CAD assembly here, with all STL files for 3D printing included in the
repo
.
This is an interactive 3D model - click and drag to rotate, scroll to zoom
Manual control
With the hardware ready, the next step was to feel how the tentacle moved. To simplify control, I reduced the tentacle’s three tendon lengths (a 3D space) down to two intuitive dimensions you can manipulate with a trackpad.
Concretely, each of the three tendons has a principal pulling direction in the 2D plane, forming a triangular basis that sums to zero. By projecting the 2D cursor control vector onto each tendon’s principal axis, you compute how much each tendon should shorten or lengthen to align with the desired direction.
This projection is linear:
$$
s_i = \mathbf{v}_i^\top \mathbf{c}
$$
where:
$\mathbf{c}$ is the 2D cursor vector,
$\mathbf{v}_i$ is the principal axis of tendon $i$.
Positive $s_i$ means shortening the tendon; negative means lengthening it. In practice, the cursor input is normalized to keep the motor commands in a reasonable range.
While this 2D mapping doesn’t expose the tentacle’s full configuration space (there are internal shapes it cannot reach), it is intuitive. Anyone can immediately move the tentacle by dragging on a trackpad, seeing the tip follow the cursor in the same direction.
Unexpectedly, this simple 2D-to-3D mapping became the backbone of the entire system. Later, all automated control policies, from hardcoded primitives to reinforcement learning, reused the same projection layer to output actions.
Trackpad control
System design

data.title: Adding lookbehinds to rust-lang/regex
data.author: emschwartz
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在Rust的正则表达式引擎中添加无捕获的无限长度向后断言（captureless lookbehinds）。与传统只能处理有限长度的正则引擎不同，Rust的这次改进支持了无界长度的向后断言，允许匹配前面不确定长度的字符而不捕获。例如，正则`(?<=Title:\s+)\w+`可以匹配`Title: HelloWorld`中的`HelloWorld`。然而，该功能不支持捕获组。

Rust的正则引擎架构由多个组件组成，包括`regex-syntax`负责解析正则表达式为抽象语法树（AST）和高级中间表示（HIR），以及`regex-automata`提供不同实现的正则引擎，如PikeVM。本次改进主要在PikeVM中增加了两个新的NFA状态类型`WriteLookAround`和`CheckLookAround`，以支持向后断言的匹配和检查。通过这些改动，Rust的正则引擎实现了对无捕获向后断言的线性时间匹配支持。

44572273.article_content:
An annotated guide to adding captureless lookbehinds to the Rust linear-time regex engine.
In a
previous blogpost
, Erik wrote about how he implemented
the linear time matching algorithm from
[RegElk+PLDI24]
in the popular regex engine RE2.
In this one, we're looking at how to do the same thing for the official regex engine from
the Rust language. Namely, we add support for unbounded captureless lookbehinds.
[
RegElk+PLDI24
]
[PLDI ’24]
Linear Matching of JavaScript Regular Expressions
(RegElk)
Aurèle Barrière
,
Clément Pit-Claudel
Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages
(
PLDI 2024
).
First, let's discover the newly supported feature and its limitations.
Lookbehinds allow regexes to make assertions about things preceding some part of the
regex pattern without considering it as part of the match. Similarly, negative lookbehinds,
which we also support, assert that something is not preceding. Consider the regex
(?<=Title:\s+)\w+
which would match the following strings (matches underlined with
~
):
Title: HelloWorld
~~~~~~~~~~
Title: Title: foo
~~~~~
~~~
But does not match:
No heading
title: bad case
Title:nospace
As seen in the example, lookbehind expression can be unbounded. This means we do not know ahead
of time how many characters a lookbehind will match. This is an improvement over many existing
regex engines which support lookbehinds but only if they are of a bounded
(like the ubiquitous
PCRE
)
or sometimes even fixed (like Python's
re
) length.
However, as a downside our lookbehinds do not support containing capture groups which are a
feature allowing to extract a substring that matched a part of the regex pattern.
The actual implementation can be found in the
PR
to the
rust-lang/regex repository.
Architecture of the regex crate
In the Rust ecosystem, libraries that are published are called crates. The language team
maintains a handful of official crates, among which there is one called "regex" that provides
exactly what you would expect: a regex matching engine.
Under the hood, the
regex crate
is only a thin wrapper around the much more elaborate
"regex-automata" crate, which provides several different engine implementations to match
regexes. Furthermore, the code for parsing regexes is split into yet another crate called
"regex-syntax". In the following, we will give an overview of the architecture of
both these crates.
Regex-Syntax
This crate takes care of processing the raw regex input into a representation that can be
easily used by the regex compiler. The first step is to parse the string representing a
regex into the AST (abstract syntax tree) representation. At this stage all unsupported
regex features are rejected, such as backreferences. Then, the AST is translated into
a more normalized representation called HIR (high-level intermediate representation).
Each node in the HIR stores properties which help the compiler and the engines
to optimize or guarantee correctness of the regex matching process. An example of such a
property is the length of the shortest and longest string that can be matched by
the HIR node.
Regex-Automata
This crate features many different implementations of a regex engine, each with different
capabilities and runtime characteristics. All engines promise to have linear runtime
complexity (in the length of the haystack and size of the regex), but the constant factors
differ. The main engine that we modified for our implementation is the PikeVM which performs
extended NFA simulation.
However, there is one other engine in this crate that is of great importance: the meta-regex.
This engine is what is used by the wrapping top-level "regex" crate and its job is to select
the "best" of the other engines for performing a search. This decision procedure is based on
some heuristics that don't matter much for understanding our work, but one important detail
is that the engine first tries to find a match without using any regex engine if possible.
This is the case when the regex consists of only a literal character sequence or a disjunction
of multiple such sequences or if it can be transformed into such a disjunction.
A match can then be searched by a "simple" substring search.
Implementation work
Most of the initial work to get lookbehinds up and running consisted of implementing the two
new NFA state types "WriteLookAround" and "CheckLookAround" (
code
).
The first is essentially the equivalent of a "match" state but for a lookbehind, while the
second instructs the regex engine to check whether or not a certain lookbehind matches at
the current string position. We named them "*LookAround" instead of "*LookBehind" because,
in principle, they are enough to implement lookaheads as well. In this section and the
following sub-sections, we will dive deeper into the used lookbehind algorithm and the issues
that arise from it.
Once these states were properly produced by the
regex-parser
and
compiler pipeline
,
and once we told the
PikeVM
how to interpret these instructions, we ha

data.title: Reflections on OpenAI
data.author: calvinfo
data.article_summary: Calvin French-Owen回顾了他在OpenAI工作一年的经历，强调了这家快速成长的公司独特的文化和挑战。OpenAI在短短一年内从1,000人扩展到3,000人，导致沟通、产品发布和人员管理等方面的问题。公司内部高度依赖Slack，几乎没有电子邮件。OpenAI的文化自下而上，好主意可以来自任何人，研究进展通过迭代产生。公司偏向行动，常有多个团队同时进行类似项目。研究人员像“ mini-executive” 一样独立工作，偏好解决新问题。管理层调整方向迅速，重视根据新信息做出正确决策。French-Owen认为，尽管个人渴望新的开始，但OpenAI的工作影响深远，尤其是参与AGI和LLM的开发，令他感到幸运。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的企业文化、工作强度与可持续性、产品研发方向与决策、对外界批评的回应、与竞争对手的比较等。

不同观点：
• **企业文化与创新机制**：
  - **[fidotron]** 认为OpenAI的创新往往是通过“nerd-sniping”方式，由研究人员对特定问题的兴趣驱动，而不是自上而下的计划。这可能导致一些被视为无聊或已解决的问题得不到关注，但也可能成为他们的弱点。
  - **[humbleferret]** 指出OpenAI的进步是迭代的，由下至上的，好的想法可以来自任何地方，并且领导层是基于执行力和想法质量晋升的，而不是政治技巧。

• **工作强度与可持续性**：
  - **[bhl]** 描述了在OpenAI工作的强度极高，每天工作到深夜，周末也经常加班，这引发了对其长期可持续性的担忧，尤其是在防止员工倦怠方面。
  - **[hinterlands]** 认为文章中对工作的积极评价不常见，但提醒说，这种高强度的工作环境可能让一些人感到没有方向，缺乏明确的愿景和路线图。

• **产品研发与外界影响**：
  - **[humbleferret]** 提到OpenAI的产品深受公众情绪影响，公司的运行在某种程度上依赖于“twitter上的氛围”。此外，GPU的高昂成本改变了公司的财务和工程优先级。
  - **[tptacek]** 表示对OpenAI在产品研发过程中如何使用LLM（大规模语言模型）感兴趣，但文章中未详细提及这一点。

• **对外界批评的回应**：
  - **[hinterlands]** 指出，尽管OpenAI在媒体上受到批评，但文章中强调公司内的人都在努力做正确的事，这与其他公司类似。然而，这种“正确的事”往往是员工对自己有益的决策进行合理化解释。

• **与竞争对手的比较**：
  - **[jjani]** 认为OpenAI在分发AI利益方面确实有所实践，但与其他竞争者（如Anthropic和Google）相比，OpenAI在API访问和模型透明性方面存在不足，如身份验证严格、模型推断计算不透明等。

补充讨论：
• **招聘与宣传**：
  - **[dagorenouf]** 怀疑文章是否是为了招聘而发布的“过于美好”的宣传。
  - **[seydor]** 认为文章可能是对Meta的暗讽。

• **技术与基础设施**：
  - **[upghost]** 提到文章中未涉及AI辅助编码的使用情况，并对OpenAI在Azure上的依赖及其对基础设施的影响表示关注。
  - **[nembal]** 好奇如果OpenAI不依赖于Azure，其基础设施是否会更具弹性和效率。

• **其他**：
  - **[randometc]** 对文章中提到的GTM角色表示困惑，希望了解其具体含义。

争议焦点：
- OpenAI的企业文化是否真正具有包容性和方向性，还是过于混乱和缺乏明确的愿景。
- 工作强度和可持续性的平衡问题。
- 与其他竞争者相比，OpenAI在透明性和模型访问方面的表现。

44573195.article_content:
Reflections on OpenAI
Calvin French-Owen
/
Writing
Calvin French-Owen
About
Writing
Bookshelf
Reflections on OpenAI
JUL 15, 2025
I left
OpenAI
three weeks ago. I had joined the company back in May 2024.
I wanted to share my reflections because there's a lot of smoke and noise around what OpenAI is doing, but not a lot of first-hand accounts of what the culture of working there actually
feels like
.
Nabeel Quereshi
has an amazing post called
Reflections on Palantir
, where he ruminates on what made Palantir special. I wanted to do the same for OpenAI while it's fresh in my mind. You won't find any trade secrets here, more just reflections on this current iteration of one of the most fascinating organizations in history at an extremely interesting time.
To put it up-front: there wasn't any personal drama in my decision to leave–in fact I was deeply conflicted about it. It's hard to go from being a
founder of your own thing
to an employee at a 3,000-person organization. Right now I'm craving a fresh start.
It's entirely possible that the quality of the work will draw me back. It's hard to imagine building anything as impactful as AGI, and LLMs are easily the technological innovation of the decade. I feel lucky to have seen some of the developments first-hand and also been a part of the
Codex launch
.
Obviously these aren't the views of the company–as observations they are my own. OpenAI is a big place, and this is my little window into it.
Culture
The first thing to know about OpenAI is
how quickly it's grown
. When I joined, the company was a little over 1,000 people. One year later, it is over 3,000 and I was in the top 30% by tenure. Nearly everyone in leadership is doing a drastically different job than they were ~2-3 years ago.
1
Of course,
everything breaks
when you scale that quickly: how to communicate as a company, the reporting structures, how to ship product, how to manage and organize people, the hiring processes, etc. Teams vary significantly in culture: some are sprinting flat-out all the time, others are babysitting big runs, some are moving along at a much more consistent pace. There's no single OpenAI experience, and
research
,
applied
, and
GTM
operate on very different time horizons.
An unusual part of OpenAI is that
everything, and I mean
everything
, runs on Slack
. There is no email. I maybe received ~10 emails in my entire time there. If you aren't organized, you will find this incredibly distracting. If you curate your channels and notifications, you can make it pretty workable.
OpenAI is
incredibly bottoms-up, especially in research
. When I first showed up, I started asking questions about the roadmap for the next quarter. The answer I got was: "this doesn't exist" (though now it does). Good ideas can come from anywhere, and it's often not really clear which ideas will prove most fruitful ahead of time. Rather than a grand 'master plan', progress is iterative and uncovered as new research bears fruit.
Thanks to this bottoms-up culture, OpenAI is also
very meritocratic
. Historically, leaders in the company are promoted primarily based upon their ability to have good ideas and then execute upon them. Many leaders who were incredibly competent weren't very good at things like presenting at all-hands or political maneuvering. That matters less at OpenAI then it might at other companies. The best ideas do tend to win.
2
There's a
strong bias to action
(you can just do things). It wasn't unusual for similar teams but unrelated teams to converge on various ideas. I started out working on a parallel (but internal) effort similar to
ChatGPT Connectors
. There must've been ~3-4 different
Codex
prototypes floating around before we decided to push for a launch. These efforts are usually taken by a small handful of individuals without asking permission. Teams tend to quickly form around them as they show promise.
Andrey (the Codex lead) used to tell me that you should think of researchers as their
own "mini-executive"
. There is a strong bias to work on your own thing and see how it pans out. There's a corollary here–most research gets done by nerd-sniping a researcher into a particular problem. If something is considered boring or 'solved', it probably won't get worked on.
Good research managers
are insanely impactful and also incredibly limited. The best ones manage to connect the dots between many different research efforts and bring together a bigger model training. The same goes for great PMs (shoutout ae).
The
ChatGPT EMs
I worked with (Akshay, Rizzo, Sulman) were some of the coolest customers I've ever seen. It really felt like they had seen everything at this point
3
. Most of them were relatively hands-off, but hired good people and tried to make sure they were setup for success.
OpenAI
changes direction on a
dime
. This was a thing we valued a lot at Segment–it's much better to do the
right
thing as you get new information, vs decide to stay the course just because you had a plan. It's

  - **[humbleferret]** 指出OpenAI的进步是迭代的，由下至上的，好的想法可以来自任何地方，并且领导层是基于执行力和想法质量晋升的，而不是政治技巧。

• **工作强度与可持续性**：
  - **[bhl]** 描述了在OpenAI工作的强度极高，每天工作到深夜，周末也经常加班，这引发了对其长期可持续性的担忧，尤其是在防止员工倦怠方面。
  - **[hinterlands]** 认为文章中对工作的积极评价不常见，但提醒说，这种高强度的工作环境可能让一些人感到没有方向，缺乏明确的愿景和路线图。

• **产品研发与外界影响**：
  - **[humbleferret]** 提到OpenAI的产品深受公众情绪影响，公司的运行在某种程度上依赖于“twitter上的氛围”。此外，GPU的高昂成本改变了公司的财务和工程优先级。
  - **[tptacek]** 表示对OpenAI在产品研发过程中如何使用LLM（大规模语言模型）感兴趣，但文章中未详细提及这一点。

• **对外界批评的回应**：
  - **[hinterlands]** 指出，尽管OpenAI在媒体上受到批评，但文章中强调公司内的人都在努力做正确的事，这与其他公司类似。然而，这种“正确的事”往往是员工对自己有益的决策进行合理化解释。

• **与竞争对手的比较**：
  - **[jjani]** 认为OpenAI在分发AI利益方面确实有所实践，但与其他竞争者（如Anthropic和Google）相比，OpenAI在API访问和模型透明性方面存在不足，如身份验证严格、模型推断计算不透明等。

补充讨论：
• **招聘与宣传**：
  - **[dagorenouf]** 怀疑文章是否是为了招聘而发布的“过于美好”的宣传。
  - **[seydor]** 认为文章可能是对Meta的暗讽。

• **技术与基础设施**：
  - **[upghost]** 提到文章中未涉及AI辅助编码的使用情况，并对OpenAI在Azure上的依赖及其对基础设施的影响表示关注。
  - **[nembal]** 好奇如果OpenAI不依赖于Azure，其基础设施是否会更具弹性和效率。

• **其他**：
  - **[randometc]** 对文章中提到的GTM角色表示困惑，希望了解其具体含义。

争议焦点：
- OpenAI的企业文化是否真正具有包容性和方向性，还是过于混乱和缺乏明确的愿景。
- 工作强度和可持续性的平衡问题。
- 与其他竞争者相比，OpenAI在透明性和模型访问方面的表现。

data.title: Designing for the Eye: Optical Corrections in Architecture and Typography
data.author: ArmageddonIt
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了建筑和字体设计中的光学修正（或光学调整），强调视觉设计需考虑光学错觉。文章以Müller-Lyer错觉为例，说明两条等长线因箭头方向不同而看似长度不一，这种错觉不受文化背景限制，甚至在动物界也能观察到。作者提到，视觉艺术家、字体设计师等应依赖眼睛的判断，而非单纯依靠测量。文中引用了Paul Renner的《The Art of Typography》一书，指出对于艺术家而言，没有光学错觉，他们从一开始就考虑了表象形式，并根据视觉印象工作。最终，当视觉印象与测量冲突时，应优先考虑视觉印象。

主要讨论点：微软产品的设计美学及其演变，特别是与苹果及其创始人史蒂夫·乔布斯的比较

不同观点：
• [1970-01-01]认为微软过去（如Windows和Office）的设计具有"粗野主义美学"（brutalist beauty），并且用户可以根据需要进行高度定制。然而，如今的O365和Azure等产品设计已经失去了这种美感，变得过于花哨，像"游行的小丑和烤面包机"。该评论者对微软早期设计持肯定态度，而对现代设计持批评态度。

• [soperj]引用了史蒂夫·乔布斯对微软的批评，特别是乔布斯关于微软"没有品味"的观点。该评论者强调微软的产品设计缺乏原创性，并指出微软的设计灵感大多来自于其他公司（如Xerox Parc和Braun），暗示微软的设计在美学和创新方面不如苹果。

补充讨论：
• [isodev]对文章本身表示赞赏，但没有深入讨论设计问题，属于对内容本身的正面反馈。

• 争议的焦点在于微软设计的美学价值及其演变。一方认为早期设计具有独特的粗野主义美学，而现代设计失去了这种美感；另一方则通过乔布斯的观点批评微软的设计缺乏品味和原创性。

• 例子和论据：[1970-01-01]通过将早期设计比作"牙科诊所"和现代设计比作"游行的小丑和烤面包机"来强调设计变化；[soperj]引用了乔布斯的名言来支持微软缺乏设计品味的观点，并指出了微软设计灵感的来源。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕微软设计美学的变化及其与苹果的比较，涉及美学价值、原创性和用户定制化等具体问题。

Designing for the Eye
Optical Corrections in Architecture and Typography
By Niko Kitsakis, June 2025
This article highlights a special aspect of both visual design and architecture: Optical cor­rections (or optical ad­just­ments, if you prefer). If you found
my piece about legible typefaces
interesting, youâll likely enjoy this one as well. Since I included many visual examples that are size-sensitive, make sure you read this on a big screen and not your mobile device.
Optical Illusions
The MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion, pictured below, makes you think that, of two lines, one is longer than the other when in fact they are of the same length. It appears in virtually every introductory book on graphic de­sign and, of course, in books on per­ception and psy­cho­lo­gy. You might not have known it by name, but you must have seen it before:
â
â
Is the blue line on top longer than the one at the bottom? Click the arrows to find out.
It used to be said that, in order to see the illu­sion, you must have grown up in an environ­ment where lines very similar to these would explicitly appear in your everyday surroundings â in architecture and furniture, for example, or when you had played with building blocks as a kid and so on. This is, incidentally, what I too was taught at my school of visual design some decades ago. However, I always had a hard time be­liev­ing it, and according to
some new research
, this is indeed not the case: Not only can the illu­sion be per­ceived by anyone, no matter their cultural background, it even extends (to some degree) to the animal kingdom and can be ex­pe­ri­enced in a haptic version as well.
The reason why I never really believed that the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion (and others like it) would work only on people who grew up in our Western culture is that, in the first place, it seems visually far too uni­ver­sal to begin with. After all, theyâre just lines. You can draw them in the sand, and they can appear naturally in many circum­stan­ces. When I look at another person, my brain will assign certain values to the length of that personâs arms, legs, and torso, and memorise them as some variety of line as well. If the brain didnât do that, we would not be able to tell if a body or facial features were out of proportion. So in my view, something dis­cern­ible only by people from a specific culture would have to be far more elaborate than an optical illusion of just a few lines.
While that was only my personal gut-feeling, I soon dis­co­vered that other people had made similar obser­va­tions. One such time was when I first read Paul Rennerâs 1940 book
Die Kunst der Typo­grafie
(The Art of Typo­graphy). The book covers pretty much every­thing you need to know to become a typo­graph­er, in­clu­ding that you should not rely on mea­su­ring things but rather on what your own eyes tell you:
Der glaube an das ZÃ¤hlen und Messen verfÃ¼hrt in allen KÃ¼nsten zu den grÃ¶bsten Fehlern.
The belief in counting and measuring leads to the grossest errors in all the arts.
Renner happens to show the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion in his book and writes about what to make of it and other visual illusions like it. Take a look at this book spread first:
If you read books, you have an advantage.
If you look closely, you can see a version of the MÃ¼ller-Lyer illusion in the top right box of the left page. Renner describes every optical illu­sion on that page separately, but whatâs interesting is how he con­clu­des that section. He says that the following applies to all of the optical illusions:
FÃ¼r die Anschauungsweise des KÃ¼nstlers, des Schriftschneiders und des Typographen gibt es hier keine optischen TÃ¤uschungen, sie rechnen von vornherein mit den scheinbaren Formen; was scheinbar falsch ist, ist fÃ¼r sie falsch; und was scheinbar richtig ist, ist fÃ¼r sie richtig. Es handelt sich also nicht darum, ein genaues ZÃ¤hlen, Messen und Bauen durch ein unbestimmtes, schwankendes, willkÃ¼rliches GefÃ¼hl, das niemand nach­prÃ¼fen kann, zu ersetzen, sondern man soll einfach den wirklichen Augenschein, dessen Feststellung ein sehr geÃ¼btes Auge erfordert, als maÃgeblich anerkennen; er ist zwar âsubjektivâ, aber er ist, wie die Gelehrten sagen, âintersubjektiv gleichâ, also bei allen Menschen den gleichen TÃ¤uschungen unterworfen. Da alle bildende Kunst fÃ¼r den Augenschein arbeitet, so mÃ¼ssen wir ihm Ã¼berall dort recht geben, wo er mit der Zahl und der Messung in Widerspruch gerÃ¤t.
From the perspective of the artist, the punchcutter, and the typographer, there are no optical illusions here â they assume from the outset the apparent forms; what appears false is false for them, and what appears correct is correct for them. It is therefore not a matter of replacing precise counting, measuring, and constructing with a vague, fluctuating, arbitrary feeling that no one can verify, but rather of simply recognising the actual visual impression â whose assessment requires a very well-trained eye â as autho­ri

data.title: Blender 4.5 LTS Released
data.author: obdev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Blender软件的发展、功能更新、技术支持及其在3D内容创作领域的地位

不同观点：
• [unshavedyak] 认为Blender提供了很多价值，鼓励大家通过每月捐款支持其发展，哪怕只是一点点帮助也会有很大作用。
• [_bent] 强调了自定义网格法线功能的重要性，并指出通过OSL定义自定义相机功能非常有趣，可以实现更物理准确的镜头模拟和更有趣的背景虚化效果，相比标准相机模型有显著优势。
• [raincole] 认为Blender正在迅速占领3D内容创作领域，尽管Maya仍是行业标准的动画软件，Houdini在几何节点上更强大，但Blender的进步显著。他还提出了对未来因生成式AI的发展而导致3D内容创作工具消失的担忧。
• [JKCalhoun] 提到Blender受益于LLMs（大型语言模型）的帮助，尤其是在学习使用Blender时。他还预测未来LLM可能会更深入地集成到用户界面中，甚至成为复杂应用的必要接口。
• [obdev] 简单提到了Blender 4.5 LTS版本的发布说明，引导读者查看官方文档。
• [marcodiego] 讨论了Blender在不同操作系统上对HDR支持的情况，指出Windows上不支持HDR，Linux上仅Wayland支持，并对这种现代功能的独占性表示满意，同时纠正了自己之前关于开发版本的错误信息。
• [robertoandred] 批评了Blender官方网站的性能问题，指出其页面加载非常缓慢和卡顿。

补充讨论：
- Blender的功能进步，特别是自定义网格法线和自定义相机的技术细节。
- Blender在不同操作系统上的技术限制和支持情况，特别是HDR和Wayland的相关讨论。
- 对未来技术趋势（如LLM和生成式AI）对Blender及整个3D内容创作领域的潜在影响。
- 对Blender官网性能问题的批评。

data.title: Petabit-class transmission over > 1000 km using standard 19-core optical fiber
data.author: the_arun
data.article_summary: 2025年5月29日，日本信息通信研究机构（NICT）与住友电工株式会社合作，使用自主研发的19芯光纤实现了传输速率1.02 PB/s、传输距离1,808公里的世界纪录。该光纤具有标准包层直径0.125毫米，低损耗且兼容现有光纤基础设施。通过开发新型光放大中继技术，研究团队成功实现了超过1,000公里的长距离高容量传输，创下容量-距离积1.86 Ebits/s×km的纪录。这一成果标志着长距离、大容量光通信技术取得重大突破，为未来网络扩展和应对数据需求增长奠定了基础。研究结果已在第48届光纤通信会议（OFC 2025）上发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于19芯光纤技术及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **throw0101c**：提到在NANOG会议中，Richard Steenbergen有一个关于光网络的演讲，并分享了去年的视频链接。这个评论主要提供信息，没有表达具体立场。

• **eqvinox**：指出文章的"highlights"部分错误地将19芯光纤称为"标准"光纤。实际上，该光纤的直径是标准的（125µm），而19芯并非标准。评论者认为多芯光纤技术正在成熟，但对"标准"的误用提出了质疑。

• **exabrial**：提出一个问题，比较了以太网LAG组和多芯光纤的带宽组合方式。LAG组中单个TCP流受限于单条链路的速度，而多芯光纤似乎能将多条光纤组合成一个更快的流。评论者对这种技术差异表示疑惑，并询问为何在以太网中不能实现类似的效果。

• **aDfbrtVt**：认为19芯光纤主要是一个高芯数弱耦合光纤的概念验证，特别是来自Sumitomo的产品。同时指出文中未提及MIMO增益的具体数据，并认为19通道MIMO接收结构在实际应用中不切实际。

• **bcrl**：指出19芯光纤并非行业标准，12芯的倍数才是电信行业的黄金标准。提到当前高计数光缆通常使用更灵活的结构，以提高密度并保持标准工具的兼容性。

补充讨论：
• **ksec**：提供了关于光纤传输距离的具体数据（1,808公里），并通过与美国地理宽度的比较，帮助理解这一距离的实际意义。

争议焦点：
• 19芯光纤是否为标准以及其在实际应用中的可行性和实用性是讨论的主要争议点。eqvinox、aDfbrtVt和bcrl都对此提出了质疑和批评，而throw0101c和ksec则更关注信息的提供和实际数据的分享。

• 另一个争议点是多芯光纤技术与传统以太网LAG组在带宽组合上的差异，exabrial对此表示不解，并寻求技术上的解释。

World Record Achieved in Transmission Capacity and Distance: With 19-core Optical Fiber with Standard Cladding Diameter 1,808 km Transmission of 1.02 Petabits per Second
- Expectation for Future Long-Distance High-Capacity Optical Communication Infrastructure -
May 29, 2025
(Japanese version released on April 24, 2025)
National Institute of Information and Communications Technology
Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd.
Highlights
The world's first successful petabit-class transmission over more than 1,000 km using standard 19-core optical fiber, achieving a transmission rate of 1.02 petabits per second over a distance of 1,808 km.
Achieved using a newly developed standard 19-core optical fiber, equivalent to 19 standard fibers, low loss across multiple wavelength bands, and the development of an optical amplification relay function compatible with this fiber.
This is a major step to realize future long-distance, large-capacity optical communication systems.
An
international research team
led by the Photonic Network Laboratory at the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT, President: TOKUDA Hideyuki Ph.D.), and including Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. (Sumitomo Electric, President: INOUE Osamu) have set a new world record in optical fiber communications, achieving data transmission at 1.02
petabits
per second over a distance of 1,808 kilometers (roughly equivalent to the distance from Sapporo to Fukuoka, from Missouri to Montana or from Berlin to Naples). The experiment used a specially designed 19-core optical fiber with a
standard 0.125 mm cladding diameter
, compatible with existing fiber infrastructure. With a
capacity-distance product
of 1.86 exabits per second x km—the
highest ever recorded
—this demonstration marks the fastest long-distance transmission achieved in any optical fiber to date. The result represents a major step forward in developing scalable, high-capacity networks and addressing the world’s growing demand for data.
A standard cladding diameter 19-core optical fiber has been demonstrated to transmit more than 1 petabit per second in the past, but over relatively short distances, well below 1,000 km. The research team has achieved a dramatic extension of the transmission distance by developing a novel 19-core optical fiber also with a standard cladding diameter but with low loss across multiple wavelength bands used in commercial optical fiber transmission systems. In addition, an optical amplification system was developed to support the new optical fiber, which enabled a world record for long-distance high-capacity transmission. The newly developed technology is expected to make a significant contribution to both the expansion of the communication capacity and the long-range extension of optical communication infrastructure in the future, when communication demand increases.
The results of this experiment were accepted as a post-deadline paper presentation at the 48th Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC 2025) and presented on Thursday, April 3, 2025.

44546321.article_summary: 2025年5月29日，日本信息通信研究机构（NICT）与住友电工株式会社合作，使用自主研发的19芯光纤实现了传输速率1.02 PB/s、传输距离1,808公里的世界纪录。该光纤具有标准包层直径0.125毫米，低损耗且兼容现有光纤基础设施。通过开发新型光放大中继技术，研究团队成功实现了超过1,000公里的长距离高容量传输，创下容量-距离积1.86 Ebits/s×km的纪录。这一成果标志着长距离、大容量光通信技术取得重大突破，为未来网络扩展和应对数据需求增长奠定了基础。研究结果已在第48届光纤通信会议（OFC 2025）上发布。
44546321.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于19芯光纤技术及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **throw0101c**：提到在NANOG会议中，Richard Steenbergen有一个关于光网络的演讲，并分享了去年的视频链接。这个评论主要提供信息，没有表达具体立场。

• **eqvinox**：指出文章的"highlights"部分错误地将19芯光纤称为"标准"光纤。实际上，该光纤的直径是标准的（125µm），而19芯并非标准。评论者认为多芯光纤技术正在成熟，但对"标准"的误用提出了质疑。

• **exabrial**：提出一个问题，比较了以太网LAG组和多芯光纤的带宽组合方式。LAG组中单个TCP流受限于单条链路的速度，而多芯光纤似乎能将多条光纤组合成一个更快的流。评论者对这种技术差异表示疑惑，并询问为何在以太网中不能实现类似的效果。

• **aDfbrtVt**：认为19芯光纤主要是一个高芯数弱耦合光纤的概念验证，特别是来自Sumitomo的产品。同时指出文中未提及MIMO增益的具体数据，并认为19通道MIMO接收结构在实际应用中不切实际。

• **bcrl**：指出19芯光纤并非行业标准，12芯的倍数才是电信行业的黄金标准。提到当前高计数光缆通常使用更灵活的结构，以提高密度并保持标准工具的兼容性。

补充讨论：
• **ksec**：提供了关于光纤传输距离的具体数据（1,808公里），并通过与美国地理宽度的比较，帮助理解这一距离的实际意义。

争议焦点：
• 19芯光纤是否为标准以及其在实际应用中的可行性和实用性是讨论的主要争议点。eqvinox、aDfbrtVt和bcrl都对此提出了质疑和批评，而throw0101c和ksec则更关注信息的提供和实际数据的分享。

• 另一个争议点是多芯光纤技术与传统以太网LAG组在带宽组合上的差异，exabrial对此表示不解，并寻求技术上的解释。

data.author: sagarkava
data.article_summary: VideoSDK AI Agents 是一个开源框架，用于开发实时多模态对话AI代理。该框架基于VideoSDK的Python SDK，允许AI代理以参与者身份加入VideoSDK会议，实现语音和媒体的实时互动。主要功能包括实时音视频通信、SIP电话集成、虚拟化身、多模型支持（如OpenAI、Gemini）、 cascading pipeline（集成STT、LLM、TTS）、对话流管理、功能工具扩展（如事件调度、费用跟踪）以及MCP和A2A协议集成。使用前需准备VideoSDK认证令牌、会议ID、Python 3.12及以上版本和第三方API密钥。通过安装核心包和可选插件，用户可以创建自定义代理，并通过继承Agent类定义代理的个性、能力及入会消息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VideoSDK实时AI代理的发布及其技术实现和优势

不同观点：
• Sagar（VideoSDK联合创始人）认为当前的语音代理开发存在诸多问题，如声音机械化、回答不准确以及缺乏可观察性，这些问题通常源于开发者需要拼凑不同的技术（如STT、LLM、TTS）并依赖HTTP端点。
• 他提出VideoSDK的解决方案，通过提供低延迟的全球WebRTC基础设施和多种功能模块（如原生轮次检测、VAD、噪声抑制、实时模型切换等），来解决上述问题。

补充讨论：
• VideoSDK的特性包括模块化管道、内置RAG和记忆功能以防止语音代理出现“幻觉”和回答不准确的问题。
• 提供多种SDK支持（如web、移动、Unity、IoT和电话），且无需粘合代码，同时具备Agent Cloud以实现一键部署和无限扩展，或者可以选择自托管以获得完全控制。
• Sagar邀请社区提出想法和问题，并表示愿意深入讨论架构、使用案例以及复杂的边缘案例。

争议焦点：
目前在该评论中未见明显争议，主要为产品发布和其技术优势的介绍。然而，潜在争议可能包括用户对开放源代码解决方案的实际效果和易用性的验证，以及与其他类似技术（如现有商业语音代理系统）的比较。

VideoSDK AI Agents
Open-source framework for developing real-time multimodal conversational AI agents.
Overview
The AI Agent SDK is a Python framework built on top of the VideoSDK Python SDK that enables AI-powered agents to join VideoSDK rooms as participants. This SDK serves as a real-time bridge between AI models (like OpenAI and Gemini) and your users, facilitating seamless voice and media interactions.
#
Feature
Description
1
🎤 Real-time Communication (Audio/Video)
Agents can listen, speak, and interact live in meetings.
2
📞 SIP & Telephony Integration
Seamlessly connect agents to phone systems via SIP for call handling, routing, and PSTN access.
3
🧍 Virtual Avatars
Add lifelike avatars to enhance interaction and presence using Simli.
4
🤖 Multi-Model Support
Integrate with OpenAI, Gemini, AWS NovaSonic, and more.
5
🧩 Cascading Pipeline
Integrates with different providers of STT, LLM, and TTS seamlessly.
6
🧠 Conversational Flow
Manages turn detection and VAD for smooth interactions.
7
🛠️ Function Tools
Extend agent capabilities with event scheduling, expense tracking, and more.
8
🌐 MCP Integration
Connect agents to external data sources and tools using Model Context Protocol.
9
🔗 A2A Protocol
Enable agent-to-agent interactions for complex workflows.
Important
Star VideoSDK Repositories
⭐️
Get instant notifications for new releases and updates. Your support helps us grow and improve VideoSDK!
Architecture
This architecture shows how AI voice agents connect to VideoSDK meetings. The system links your backend with VideoSDK's platform, allowing AI assistants to interact with users in real-time.
Pre-requisites
Before you begin, ensure you have:
A VideoSDK authentication token (generate from
app.videosdk.live
)
A VideoSDK meeting ID (you can generate one using the
Create Room API
or through the VideoSDK dashboard)
Python 3.12 or higher
Third-Party API Keys:
API keys for the services you intend to use (e.g., OpenAI for LLM/STT/TTS, ElevenLabs for TTS, Google for Gemini etc.).

Create and activate a virtual environment with Python 3.12 or higher.
macOS / Linux
python3 -m venv venv
source

venv

ctivate
Install the core VideoSDK AI Agent package
pip install videosdk-agents
Install Optional Plugins. Plugins help integrate different providers for Realtime, STT, LLM, TTS, and more. Install what your use case needs:
#
Example: Install the Turn Detector plugin
pip install videosdk-plugins-turn-detector
👉 Supported plugins (Realtime, LLM, STT, TTS, VAD, Avatar, SIP) are listed in the
Supported Libraries
section below.
Generating a VideoSDK Meeting ID
Before your AI agent can join a meeting, you'll need to create a meeting ID. You can generate one using the VideoSDK Create Room API:

data.title: Mira Murati's AI startup Thinking Machines raises $2B in A16Z-led round
data.author: spenvo
data.article_summary: Thinking Machines Lab，由前OpenAI高管Mira Murati创立的AI初创公司，近日宣布完成约20亿美元融资，估值达120亿美元。此轮融资由Andreessen Horowitz领投，Nvidia、Accel、ServiceNow等参投。尽管公司今年2月才成立，且尚未有收入或产品，但Murati成功吸引了大量投资。公司计划打造更安全、可靠的AI系统，其团队近三分之二为前OpenAI员工。Murati的离职和创立新公司反映了AI领域高管的争夺战，而投资者对AI初创企业的热情依然高涨，推动美国初创企业融资在2025年上半年激增。

July 15 (Reuters) - Thinking Machines Lab, the artificial intelligence startup founded by former OpenAI executive Mira Murati, said on Tuesday it has raised about $2 billion at a valuation of $12 billion in a funding round led by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.
The fundraise also saw participation from AI chip giant Nvidia
(NVDA.O)
, opens new tab
, Accel, ServiceNow
(NOW.N)
, opens new tab

(CSCO.O)
, opens new tab

(AMD.O)
, opens new tab
and Jane Street, the startup said.
Sign up
here.
The massive funding round for a company launched only in February, with no revenue or products yet, underscores Murati's ability to attract investors in a sector where top executives have become coveted targets in an escalating talent war.
"We're excited that in the next couple months we will be able to share our first product, which will include a significant open source component and be useful for researchers and startups developing custom model," CEO Murati said in a
post
, opens new tab
on the X social media platform.
Reuters had
reported
in April Andreessen Horowitz was in talks to lead an outsized early-stage funding round.
Thinking Machines has said it wants to build artificial intelligence systems that are safer, more reliable and aimed at a broader number of applications than rivals. Nearly two-thirds of its team
at launch
comprised of former OpenAI employees.
Murati, who started Thinking Machines after an abrupt exit from OpenAI last September, is among a growing list of former executives from the ChatGPT maker who have launched AI startups.
Another two, Dario Amodei's Anthropic and Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence, have attracted former OpenAI researchers and raised billions of dollars in funding.
Investor enthusiasm toward new AI startups has stayed strong, despite some questions about tech industry spending.
That helped U.S. startup
funding surge nearly 76%
to $162.8 billion in the first half of 2025, with AI accounting for about 64.1% of the total deal value, according to a Pitchbook report.

data.title: KDE's official Roku/Android TV alternative is back from the dead
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: KDE项目Plasma Bigscreen正在复活，该项目是一个用于电视的Plasma界面，最初支持已停止更新的Mycroft AI助手。由于长期贡献者Devin花费一周时间进行全面改造，Plasma Bigscreen得以重生。Devin清理了代码库，重新设计了界面，取消了面板背景，并增加了背景模糊效果。他还添加了搜索视图，使用KRunner快速查找和启动应用程序，并重做了设置应用，采用了两栏设计。显示模块和Wi-Fi、KDE Connect模块也得到了修复和更新。虽然项目尚未完成，但目标是将其重新纳入Plasma的官方发布计划，可能在6.5版本中实现。用户可以在Raspberry Pi上通过postmarketOS测试该项目。

44573752.article_content:
Lately, some KDE projects have seen a revival, like
Karton (the native virtual machine manager for KDE)
and the
improved ISO Image Writer.
Now, another abandoned KDE project, Plasma Bigscreen, is looking to return from the dead after long-time Plasma Mobile contributor Devin decided to spend a week overhauling the thing.
If you have not heard of it,
Plasma Bigscreen
is a Plasma shell for televisions, with original support for the now-defunct Mycroft AI assistant. It used to provide a simple launcher for apps and custom "Mycroft Skills" before development stalled, causing most distributions to drop it.
The project was left behind during the big transition to Plasma 6 last year because no one had ported it in time for the megarelease. After a friend of his started poking at the code,
Devin stepped in
to tackle the much-needed work.
He started by cleaning up the repository and then jumped into redesigning the interface, drawing inspiration from older Breeze mockups. The homescreen has been flattened, removing panel backgrounds. Here's a before-and-after comparison (click to enlarge):
One of the more visible changes is that the UI now has a background blur when you are navigating menus, giving focus to the foreground elements.
For actually finding what you want to run, you are no longer stuck scrolling through a long list, as Devin added a new search view, searching using KRunner to quickly find and launch applications.
The Settings application also got a complete redesign, adopting a simple two-pane look with a sidebar for categories. A lot of the settings modules (KCM) used hardcoded layouts, so Devin built a small component library for TV-focused UIs and ported everything over.
The rewritten Display KCM now uses the libkscreen backend, and the Wi-Fi and KDE Connect modules have been fixed and updated. Startup feedback for launching applications was also broken, and when you start up an application, a small animation now plays, similar to the one on Plasma Mobile.
For anyone who wants to test this out, you can do as Devin did by installing Plasma Bigscreen on a Raspberry Pi using postmarketOS, though you would have to compile it yourself or pull from the nightly repos to get the latest changes.
Applications like Kodi and
VacuumTube (smart TV version of YouTube)
work well with remote navigation, and some games like
SuperTuxKart
are playable.
Controller support exists, but getting TV remotes to work over HDMI CEC is still untested. The project is far from finished; it still needs an arrow-navigable virtual keyboard and a clearer long-term direction now that Mycroft is gone. Still, the goal is to get it back into the official Plasma release schedule, possibly for version 6.5.

data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 一项调查显示，73%的Oracle Java用户在过去三年中经历过审计。由于Oracle在2018年引入Java付费订阅，并在2023年改为按员工人数定价，导致许多用户面临高昂成本。近80%的用户已迁移或计划迁移到开源Java以避免高成本和审计风险。仅14%的用户打算继续使用Oracle的订阅模式。调查还发现，54%的组织每年花费超过10万美元解决许可不合规问题。IT资产管理者强调，管理现代软件许可的复杂性需要更多资源和高层支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oracle Java的使用及其商业模式的争议

不同观点：
• **对Oracle Java商业版用户的不解**：
  - jsiepkes认为，在不同的云平台（如AWS、Azure、RedHat）上，使用平台提供的Java版本（如Amazon的Java、Microsoft的Java、RedHat的Java）更为合适，质疑为什么还有人使用Oracle的商业Java版本。
  
• **替代方案及应对措施**：
  - hangonhn分享了他们的经验：切换到AWS Corretto并禁止Oracle/Sun Java的下载和使用，成功避免了Oracle的进一步联系。
  
• **Oracle Java商业版的价值**：
  - lijok提问使用Oracle Java相较于开源版本的优势是什么。
  - pvtmert认为Oracle的收入主要来源于一些开发者的懒惰和对Oracle支持团队的依赖，并指出在现代JDK中，过去需要付费支持的功能已经不再必要。

• **对Oracle法律问题的担忧**：
  - marshray提到即使有优秀的开源实现，重新实现JVM仍然面临巨大的法律成本，引用Google的例子说明问题的严重性。

• **对Oracle商业行为的讽刺**：
  - DonHopkins用“lawnmower”来比喻Oracle在Java争论中的影响，暗示Oracle使得这类讨论变得无意义。
  - msie以讽刺的口吻指出Oracle的行为是为了保持其CEO Larry Ellison的财富。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到Oracle Java商业版的必要性和其高成本，尤其是与开源版本和云平台提供的Java版本的对比。
- 对Oracle法律威胁的担忧以及对开发者依赖商业支持的批评也是讨论的重点。
- 一些评论通过幽默和讽刺表达了对Oracle商业行为的不满。

44573326.article_content:
Devops
4
Nearly 3 out of 4 Oracle Java users say they've been audited in the past 3 years
4
Big Red’s changes to Java licensing also inspire exodus to open source
Lindsay Clark
Tue 15 Jul 2025
//
16:16 UTC
A survey of 500 IT asset managers in organizations that use Oracle Java has found that 73 percent have been audited in the last three years.
Deal to 'save' UK colleges £45M in Oracle Java licensing fees followed audit requests
READ MORE
At the same time, nearly eight out of 10 Oracle Java users said they had migrated, or planned to shift, to open source Java to try to avoid the risk and high costs of the dominant vendor's development and runtime environments.
Oracle introduced a paid subscription for Java in September 2018, and in January 2023, it
decided to switch its pricing model
to per employee rather than per user, creating a steep price hike for many users. In July 2023, Gartner recorded users experiencing
price increases of between two and five times
when they switched to the new licensing model.
Two years later, the survey conducted by market research firm Dimensional Research showed only 14 percent of Oracle Java users intended to stick with the vendor's subscription model.
The
research
was commissioned and authored by ITAM Forum, an independent group representing IT asset managers and Azul, which provides open source Java products and services.
It points out that Oracle introduced four licensing and pricing policy changes between 2020 and 2023. "To avoid Oracle's price hikes, Java customers must upgrade to the latest Java version every three years to continue receiving free support under the Oracle Java SE Universal Subscription or otherwise migrate to an open-source alternative," the report said.
'We had to educate Oracle about our contract,' CIO says after Big Red audit
Oracle cuts support for South African energy biz Eskom in long-running licensing dispute
Only 1 in 10 Oracle Java users want to stay with Big Red
Oracle's Java price hikes push CIOs to brew new licensing strategies
The survey also revealed the cost of audits. While vendors have the right to charge for copyright-protected software, 25 percent of survey participants said complex software configurations make tracking application usage more difficult. At the same time, 29 percent of ITAM professionals reported that their organizations struggle to manage this information, especially when tracking software usage across teams or between on-premises and cloud platforms. More than half of survey participants (54 percent) said their organization spent more than $100,000 a year on resolving licensing non-compliance issues, while 27 percent said the figure was more than $500,000 a year.
"The results highlight a fundamental mismatch between the complexity of modern software licensing and the resources organizations rely on to effectively manage software compliance," said Martin Thompson, founder of the ITAM Forum.
He added that ITAM professionals need the resources and executive buy-in to ensure compliance and successful license management.
Oracle has been offered the opportunity to respond to the survey. ®

• simonw 强调希望在所有使用的操作系统上避免运行从互联网下载的未沙盒化代码，并引用了一个恶意VSCode扩展导致加密货币被盗的案例，指出开放的VSX市场缺乏审查和沙盒机制，存在安全风险。
• gnoack 介绍了Linux中的Landlock机制，指出其在C语言中缺乏简便的包装库，但在Go和Rust中有更简洁的API。他还解释了Linux中复杂性的原因在于ABI的向后兼容性保障。
• poolpOrg 偏好OpenBSD的pledge()和unveil()机制，认为其简单有效，尤其是whitelist意图而非具体系统调用的方式令人欣赏。
• aktau 认为Linux上的沙盒化过程令人困惑，虽然欣赏Landlock的无特权限制特性，但希望看到更多方法的比较，包括需要root权限的方法，如seccomp-bpf。

补充讨论：
• 01HNNWZ0MV43FF 分享了使用systemd-run进行沙盒化的详细方法，强调其无需安装新工具，并详细解释了各个选项的作用，如RestrictAddressFamilies=、SystemCallFilter=~@mount等，如何限制进程的行为和文件系统访问。这种方法利用了systemd的内置沙盒选项，提供了一种便捷且强大的沙盒化途径。
• 关于Landlock和seccomp-bpf的比较，有讨论指出Landlock是一个无特权限制的机制，而seccomp-bpf在某些情况下也可能需要对比和参考。

• 不同操作系统和环境下的沙盒机制的简便性和安全性是讨论的核心。simonw提出的开放VSX市场的安全风险问题与其他用户对具体沙盒机制的偏好和实现细节形成了对比。
• Linux中Landlock的复杂性与其ABI兼容性保障之间的权衡也是讨论的一个重点，部分用户如gnoack认为这种复杂性是必要的，而aktau则希望看到更简洁的实现和比较。

data.title: Low-quality papers based on public health data are flood scientific literature
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 一项研究发现，五个大型开放获取的健康数据库数据被用于生成数千篇低质量、公式化的论文。自2021年至2024年，使用这些数据库的论文数量从约4000篇增至11500篇，远超预期。这些论文常有模板化标题，可能由大型语言模型或“论文工厂”批量生产。特别提及的数据库包括美国国家健康与营养调查（NHANES）、英国生物银行（UK Biobank）和美国食品药品监督管理局的不良事件报告系统（FAERS）等。研究人员警告，这些低质量论文可能涌入科学文献，带来隐患，并呼吁学术界警惕这一趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对标题中的语法问题以及美国政府对公共健康数据访问限制的看法

不同观点：
• BryanBigs认为标题中的语法错误可能是故意讽刺，或者是单纯的错误。他提出了两种可能性：一种是故意通过不好的语法制造讽刺效果，另一种是无意的错误，纯粹是语法不佳。

• msarrel则没有直接回应语法问题，而是将重点转移到对美国政府政策的批评上，指出政府正在取消公众对公共健康数据的访问权限。这暗示msarrel认为政府的行为是不当的，尤其是在公共健康信息应该更透明和公开的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 评论之间存在一定的讨论错位。BryanBigs关注的是语法问题，而msarrel将话题引向对政府政策的批评，显示出两者对当前话题优先级的不同认知。

• msarrel的评论隐含了对政府政策的不满，可能认为公共健康数据的公开是重要的，而政府的限制措施与此背道而驰。

• 争议的焦点在于公众是否有权访问公共健康数据，msarrel显然对此持否定态度，而BryanBigs的评论虽然未直接涉及该问题，但其对语法的调侃可能被视为忽视了更重要的政策议题。

Data from large, open databases appear in hundreds of low quality, repetitive papers.
Credit: Artem Cherednik/iStock via Getty
Data from five large open-access health databases are being used to generate thousands of poor-quality, formulaic papers, an analysis has found. Its authors say that the surge in publications could indicate the exploitation of these databases by people using
large language models
(LLMs) to mass-produce scholarly articles, or even by
paper mills
— companies that churn out papers to order.
AI linked to explosion of low-quality biomedical research papers
The findings, posted as a preprint on medRxiv on 9 July
1
, follow an earlier study
2
that highlighted an
explosion of such papers
that used data from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). The latest analysis flags a rising number of studies featuring data from other large health databases, including the UK Biobank and the US Food and Drug Administration’s Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), which documents the side effects of drugs.
Between 2021 and 2024, the number of papers using data from these databases rose from around 4,000 to 11,500 — around 5,000 more papers than expected on the basis of previous publication trends.
The study’s authors warn that a large number of these papers — many of which have repetitive, template-like titles — are likely to be of low quality and could flood the scientific literature. Their analysis is intended as “an early warning system … so that peer reviewers, editors and researchers can understand where the vulnerabilities in the system lie”, says co-author Matt Spick, a biomedical scientist at the University of Surrey in Guildford, UK.
Unexpected growth
Spick and his colleagues analysed changes in publication counts, title wording and author affiliations for papers that were based on data from 34 open-access health databases. The team used an algorithm to predict the growth in the numbers of papers expected for each data set from 2014 to 2024 — a period during which text-generating LLM tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini became mainstream.
Biomedical paper retractions have quadrupled in 20 years — why?
When they compared their predictions with actual publication rates, the researchers identified six data sets that had significantly exceeded the growth rates predicted by the algorithm. All but one also showed a rise in the number of papers with ‘template-like’ titles. These data sets were NHANES, UK Biobank, FAERS, the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study and the Finnish genetic database FinnGen. By 2024, the number of papers using FinnGen data grew by nearly 15 times from 2021, for example, while those using FAERS increased by nearly 4 times and UK Biobank by 2.4 times over the same period.
The researchers also uncovered some dubious papers, which often linked complex health conditions to a single variable. One paper used Mendelian randomization — a technique that helps to determine whether a particular health risk factor causes a disease — to study whether drinking semi-skimmed milk could protect against depression, whereas another looked into how education levels affect someone’s chances of developing a hernia after surgery.
“A lot of those findings might be unsafe, and yet they’re also accessible to the public, and that really worries me,” says Spick.

data.title: Santa Ragione says Apple is delisting Wheels of Aurelia 'without justification'
data.author: saubeidl
data.article_summary: 意大利游戏工作室Santa Ragione指责苹果无正当理由下架其2016年视觉小说游戏《Wheels of Aurelia》，称此举损害游戏作为文化和艺术产品的价值与可持续性。尽管游戏功能齐全并符合当前技术标准，苹果仍以“过时”为由决定下架。工作室联合创始人Pietro Righi Riva表示，多次上诉未果，苹果未能提供明确解释。他批评苹果的政策迫使小型开发团队耗费资源进行不必要的更新，影响其新项目和生存。Riva还提到，苹果在数字分发市场的支配地位使其做法更加令人担忧，呼吁更多公平和多元的数字市场环境。此事令Santa Ragione对继续支持苹果平台产生疑虑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果应用商店是否应该因为应用程序不频繁更新而下架游戏，以及该游戏是否能被视为艺术作品。

不同观点：
• 第一个观点（1659447091）认为，应用商店下架游戏可能与未遵守新的兼容性和隐私政策更新有关。评论者指出，游戏可能需要进行兼容性更新以符合当前的商店政策，特别是设备分辨率的更新，以及公开数据收集和第三方依赖的信息。评论者暗示，开发者可能因为不想公开这些信息而选择不下更新，从而导致下架。

• 第二个观点（duxup）反对因不频繁更新而下架游戏的做法，认为游戏作为文化和艺术作品，应该像书籍、电影和音乐专辑一样，享有永久的文化价值。评论者承认更新问题确实存在，但不同意所有应用都需要不断更新的观点，特别是对于那些被视为艺术的游戏。

• 第三个观点（leakycap）质疑该游戏是否能被视为艺术作品，认为从游戏的视觉效果、销售策略和故事情节来看，更像是一款普通的游戏，类似于十年前的Flash游戏，不具备艺术作品应有的深度和美学价值。

补充讨论：
• 关于游戏是否属于艺术作品的讨论。duxup认为游戏可以是艺术作品，应该享有与其他艺术形式相同的地位和永久访问权。而leakycap则从游戏的实际质量和设计出发，认为该游戏缺乏艺术价值，不值得被视为艺术作品。

• 关于应用商店政策的讨论。1659447091指出，应用商店的下架决定可能与未遵守新的兼容性和隐私政策有关，特别是需要公开游戏的数据收集行为和第三方依赖信息。

争议焦点：
• 游戏是否应被视为艺术作品，以及应用商店是否有权因不频繁更新而下架游戏。duxup支持游戏作为艺术作品的观点，而leakycap则对此持怀疑态度，认为该游戏不具备足够的艺术价值。此外，1659447091的评论暗示了下架决定可能涉及隐私政策问题，这与其他评论者的观点形成了一定的讨论关系。

The Italian studio claims Apple is undermining the 'value and sustainability of games as cultural and artistic products' with the move.

developer Santa Ragione has accused Apple of undermining the "value and sustainability of games as cultural and artistic products" after the tech company informed the studio its 2016 visual novel
Wheels of Aurelia
will be pulled from the App Store without "clear justification."
Studio co-founder and director Pietro Righi Riva shared the news with Game Developer and explained
Wheels of Aurelia
will be removed from the App Store on July 25, 2025. It was apparently granted an extended grace period after Santa Ragione appealed the decision—even though those appeals were ultimately denied.
The studio has decided to make the title available free-to-download on the platform for the next 10 days to ensure as many people as possible can experience it before it is yanked from digital shelves.
Riva said Apple has so far failed to provide an adequate explanation as to why the award-winning title has been marked for removal. "Despite multiple appeals and sincere efforts to seek clarification, Apple has not provided clear justification for this removal, citing only their policy to remove apps deemed 'obsolete' or 'outdated,' despite the game being fully functional and compliant with current technical standard(s)," he explained.
Related:

"We firmly believe that removing fully functional artistic works simply due to infrequent updates undermines the value and sustainability of games as cultural and artistic products. Like books, films, and music albums, video games represent complete creative works that do not inherently require continual updates beyond maintaining basic functionality."
"This 'obsoletion' policy further reinforces a vision that does not recognize games as an art form"
After his initial email appeal was quashed, Riva explained his second appeal resulted in a phone call with a member of Apple's team who instructed them to file another appeal via a different form. In that instance, Riva underlined that
Wheels of Aurelia
"continues to function properly and meets all expectations of users, including full compatibility with Game Center and the latest screen ratios."
He also emphasized that certain video games and other creative works "do not inherently require continuous updates beyond ensuring functionality and compliance with current regulation and technological requirements."
"Updating
Wheels of Aurelia
at this stage would demand very significant resources solely to refresh engine and SDK elements without providing meaningful enhancements to user experience or artistic value," he added in that second appeal, the contents of which were shared with Game Developer.
Related:
Report: Candy Crush maker King is allegedly replacing laid off employees with AI tools
"For smaller development teams, such forced updates represent a substantial financial burden, diverting limited resources from new projects or critical ongoing work. Alternatively, removing these titles from the App Store impacts developers' portfolios and visibility, ultimately affecting their sustainability and recognition in a very competitive industry."
Riva then received a message explaining that Santa Ragione's appeal was being evaluated. He claims it was rejected five minutes later.
Riva feels Apple's approach to delisting titles it has deemed "outdated" leaves smaller developers at risk of needing to continuously update projects to meet vague demands, costing them time and money that might otherwise be spent supporting other projects or kickstarting new endeavors.
In addition, he says Apple's "dominant position in digital distribution makes those practices especially troubling" and reinforces the importance of diversified ecosystems. "We commend recent EU regulations designed to prevent monopolistic behaviors, fostering more fairness and plurality in the digital marketplace," he added.
As for whether the situation will impact Santa Ragione's plans to support Apple platforms moving forward, Riva said the team was already discouraged by the company's shift away from human curation and questioned whether it is actually committed to helping game developers succeed.

• 关于游戏是否属于艺术作品的讨论。duxup认为游戏可以是艺术作品，应该享有与其他艺术形式相同的地位和永久访问权。而leakycap则从游戏的实际质量和设计出发，认为该游戏缺乏艺术价值，不值得被视为艺术作品。

• 关于应用商店政策的讨论。1659447091指出，应用商店的下架决定可能与未遵守新的兼容性和隐私政策有关，特别是需要公开游戏的数据收集行为和第三方依赖信息。

争议焦点：
• 游戏是否应被视为艺术作品，以及应用商店是否有权因不频繁更新而下架游戏。duxup支持游戏作为艺术作品的观点，而leakycap则对此持怀疑态度，认为该游戏不具备足够的艺术价值。此外，1659447091的评论暗示了下架决定可能涉及隐私政策问题，这与其他评论者的观点形成了一定的讨论关系。

44573622.article_content:
Finally, an LLM Router That Thinks Like an Engineer
DracattusDev
6 min read
·
Jul 8, 2025
--
1
Listen
Share
A take on “Arch-Router,” a new paper that ditches opaque quality scores for something we can actually build on: solid architectural principles.
Every so often, a paper lands on your desk that doesn’t just present a novel algorithm, but outlines an architectural philosophy that makes you nod and say, “Yes, that’s how it
should
be done.” For me, that paper is “Arch-Router: Aligning LLM Routing with Human Preferences.”
For those of us in the trenches, the past few years have been a whirlwind of integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into our products. The journey usually starts with a single, glorious model — a GPT-4 or a Claude — powering a new feature. But it never ends there. Soon, the requirements pile up. We need a model for fast, cheap conversational chat. A different one for complex code generation. Another that’s fine-tuned on legal jargon. And one more for image editing.
Suddenly, you’re not just calling an API; you’re orchestrating a fleet of specialized brains. And this brings you face-to-face with the messy, frustrating challenge of LLM routing: How do you send the right query to the right model, every single time?
Until now, we’ve been wrestling with a two-headed hydra of routing solutions, neither of them particularly satisfying.
Head #1: The Brittle Classifier.
This approach trains a model to classify a query into a predefined category (e.g., code_gen, summarization). It works, but it’s rigid. Adding a new skill or model means going back to the data, retraining the entire router, and redeploying. It’s the software equivalent of pouring concrete: strong but impossible to change.
Head #2: The Black-Box Oracle.
This is the performance-based router. It tries to predict a numerical “quality score” for how well each available model might handle a given query, often factoring in cost and latency. While appealing in theory, it’s an operational nightmare. These routers are often opaque, difficult to debug, and their quality judgments can feel arbitrary, failing to capture the subjective nuance of what a “good” response actually means for a specific user’s intent.
The Arch-Router paper steps past this dilemma and proposes a third, far more elegant path — one that feels like it was designed by someone who has actually had to maintain a complex system in production.
A Brilliant Abstraction: Separating the What from the How
The most compelling idea in Arch-Router isn’t a new neural network architecture; it’s a classic, rock-solid engineering principle:
decoupling
.
The framework splits the routing process into two distinct parts:
Route Selection:
This is the
what
. The system defines a set of human-readable routing policies using a “Domain-Action Taxonomy.” Think of it as a clear API contract written in plain English. A policy isn’t just intent_123; it’s a descriptive label like Domain: ‘finance’, Action: ‘analyze_earnings_report’. The router’s only job is to match the user’s query to the best-fit policy description.
Model Assignment:
This is the
how
. A separate, simple mapping configuration connects each policy to a specific LLM. The finance/analyze_earnings_report policy might map to a powerful model like GPT-4o, while a simpler general/greeting policy maps to a faster, cheaper model.
The core architectural idea from the paper (Figure 1). Route selection is decoupled from the actual model mapping, which is a game-changer for maintainability.
This is a profound shift. We’re moving from predicting quality to classifying intent against a stable, human-authored contract. The “quality” judgment is made upfront by the developer who defines the policies and chooses the best model for that job.
From an engineering perspective, the benefits are immediate and obvious:
Flexibility on Steroids:
Want to A/B test a new Claude model against GPT-4 for code generation? Just update the mapping file for the code_generation policy. No retraining needed. Is one of your model providers having an outage? Hot-swap the endpoint for that route in seconds.
Unprecedented Transparency:
When the router makes a decision, you know exactly why. It matched the user’s query to a specific, named policy whose description you can read. Debugging shifts from analyzing opaque model weights to auditing a clear set of routing rules.
True Maintainability:
This architecture makes the system easy to reason about and easy to evolve. New capabilities can be added by simply defining new policies and mapping them to models. The router itself, Arch-Router, doesn’t even need to be touched.
Arch-Router: A Small Engine for a Big Job
The implementation of the router itself is just as pragmatic. The authors built Arch-Router as a compact 1.5-billion parameter model. In a world chasing ever-larger models, this is a breath of fresh air. A router must be lightning-fast; it’s a gatekeeper that adds overhead to every single request. A small, efficient mode

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于气候变化的责任与应对措施

不同观点：

• 观点一：认为个人行为对气候变化影响有限，大公司和政府应承担更多责任。
  - 论据：个人改变生活方式（如减少开车、节约能源）虽然有帮助，但大公司和政府在制定政策和推动系统性变革方面具有更大影响力。
  - 例子：大公司排放大量温室气体，却常常逃避责任，而个人无论多么努力，整体影响还是微不足道。

• 观点二：强调个人责任，认为每个人都应为减缓气候变化尽一份力。
  - 论据：尽管大公司和政府确实在气候变化中扮演重要角色，但个人的努力也不可忽视，每个人都可以通过改变消费习惯、支持环保政策来做出贡献。
  - 例子：减少塑料使用、选择公共交通或自行车出行、支持可持续产品等，都是个人可以采取的实际行动。

• 观点三：质疑气候变化的真实性和科学依据。
  - 论据：认为气候变化可能被夸大或误解，质疑现有气候科学研究的可靠性。
  - 例子：引用一些未被主流科学界广泛接受的研究或观点，认为气候变化是自然现象，而非人类活动所致。

• 观点四：主张技术创新是解决气候变化的关键。
  - 论据：认为通过技术进步，如发展可再生能源、碳捕捉技术等，可以有效应对气候变化问题。
  - 例子：太阳能、风能技术的发展，以及新型电池技术的突破，都是通过技术创新解决环境问题的实例。

补充讨论：

- 争议焦点：主要集中在责任分配上，即个人、公司和政府在应对气候变化中的具体角色和责任。
- 讨论关系：观点一和观点二虽然侧重点不同，但可以互补，强调系统性变革和个人努力的结合。观点三与主流观点对立，挑战气候变化的科学共识。观点四提供了一种不同于传统环保手段的新思路，强调技术在解决问题中的潜力。

data.title: Impacts of adding PV solar system to internal combustion engine vehicles
data.author: red369
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳能应用于电动车和传统汽车的可行性及效率

不同观点：
• [支持太阳能应用于电动车，尤其是固定安装]  
Chris222展示了通过家用太阳能系统为电动车充电的成功案例，强调其经济性和环保效益。他提到两套太阳能系统年发电量超过20MWh，并通过智能充电设备调整充电速率，实现几乎零成本的出行。他认为这种方案在25年以上的生命周期内非常划算，成本约为5美分/kWh。

• [质疑车载太阳能的效率]  
Veliladon和Infecto等用户认为车载太阳能效率低下，EROEI（能量投入产出比）难以超过1，尤其是在车辆经常处于不理想的光照条件下。他们主张将太阳能板安装在房屋或建筑物顶部，以获得更大效益。Infecto进一步指出，复杂性和能量损耗（如风阻）使得车载太阳能不太实际。

• [支持小规模太阳能应用]  
Londons_explore和Throwaway3b03提到小规模太阳能应用的好处，例如防止电池长时间停放后亏电，或在传统内燃机汽车中减少寄生电池损耗。Jollyllama补充说，这可能仅对传统内燃机汽车有意义，作为解决电池亏电的临时方案。

• [具体案例与创新应用]  
Torginus分享了瑞典人利用1kW太阳能板满足日常通勤的实例。Testing22321提到一对夫妇通过携带的太阳能板完成长途旅行的案例。Qem则探讨了太阳能在长途货车运输中的潜在应用，建议利用货车大面积安装太阳能板，并调整行驶时间以最大化太阳能利用。

补充讨论：
• [技术复杂性与工程权衡]  
Janosch_123指出自制电动车中太阳能应用的技术复杂性，认为增加的复杂性带来的收益有限。Condensedcrab提到即使专门设计的Aptera车型也只能通过车顶太阳能板恢复10%的电池电量。Burnt-resistor以幽默方式提及Solar Freakin' Roadways项目，暗示其不切实际。

• [历史与未来应用]  
Ianbooker回顾了20年前太阳能天窗在传统内燃机车中的应用，而Glyptodon则设想了一种无需铅酸电池的太阳能系统，以减少维护麻烦。

争议焦点：
• 太阳能应用于电动车的主要争议在于车载太阳能的效率与复杂性，支持者强调经济与环保效益，反对者则认为固定安装更有效，且车载太阳能带来的技术挑战和能量损耗不值得。

Torginus分享了瑞典人利用1kW太阳能板满足日常通勤的实例。Testing22321提到一对夫妇通过携带的太阳能板完成长途旅行的案例。Qem则探讨了太阳能在长途货车运输中的潜在应用，建议利用货车大面积安装太阳能板，并调整行驶时间以最大化太阳能利用。

补充讨论：
• [技术复杂性与工程权衡]  
Janosch_123指出自制电动车中太阳能应用的技术复杂性，认为增加的复杂性带来的收益有限。Condensedcrab提到即使专门设计的Aptera车型也只能通过车顶太阳能板恢复10%的电池电量。Burnt-resistor以幽默方式提及Solar Freakin' Roadways项目，暗示其不切实际。

• [历史与未来应用]  
Ianbooker回顾了20年前太阳能天窗在传统内燃机车中的应用，而Glyptodon则设想了一种无需铅酸电池的太阳能系统，以减少维护麻烦。

争议焦点：
• 太阳能应用于电动车的主要争议在于车载太阳能的效率与复杂性，支持者强调经济与环保效益，反对者则认为固定安装更有效，且车载太阳能带来的技术挑战和能量损耗不值得。

data.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Django
data.author: davepeck
data.article_summary: Django迎来20周年，2005年7月13日Jacob Kaplan-Moss进行了首个公开提交。为庆祝这一里程碑，官方推出了一个20周年网站，展示2025年全球的线上和线下庆祝活动，包括生日蛋糕、Django知识测验和社区成就展示等。同时，Django软件基金会设定了一个筹款目标：在20天内吸引200名新捐赠者，其中至少20名每月捐赠，以支持项目发展。截至2025年7月13日，已筹集了76,707美元，完成了目标的25.6%。展望未来，Django计划继续发布新版本，扩展生态系统，并保持包容和支持的开发者社区。

• **赞扬Django的稳定性和职业影响**：
   - **ekinertac**：Django的稳定性、安全性和实用性使其在web开发中长盛不衰，特别适合构建实际业务。

• **强调社区和生态系统的重要性**：
   - **akoumjian**：Django社区的合作和分享精神加速了个人职业发展，并通过用户组活动增强了软件工程能力。

   - **aniforprez**：希望Django引入原生Python类型和类型提示，以提高开发体验。

44552500.article_content:
Happy 20th birthday Django!
Posted by
Thibaud Colas & Benjamin Balder Bach
on July 13, 2025
On July 13th 2005, Jacob Kaplan-Moss made the first commit to the public repository that would become Django. Twenty years and 400+ releases later, here we are –
Happy 20th birthday Django! 🎉
Join the celebrations
We want to share this special occasion with you all! Our new
20-years of Django website
showcases all online and local events happening around the world, through all of 2025. As well as other opportunities to celebrate!
Expect birthday cake 🎂 and singing Happy Birthday
A special quiz or two? see who knows all about Django trivia
Showcase of great community achievements
View our 20th birthday website
Support Django
As a birthday gift of sorts, consider whether you or your employer can support the project via donations to our non-profit Django Software Foundation. For this special event, we want to set a special goal!
Over the next 20 days, we want to see 200 new donors, supporting Django with $20 or more, with at least 20 monthly donors.
Help us making this happen:
Donate on the Django website
Donate on GitHub sponsors
Or check out how to
become a Corporate Member
Once you’ve done it, post with #DjangoBirthday and tag us
on Mastodon
/
on Bluesky
/
on X
/
on LinkedIn
so we can say thank you!
26%
Of our US $300,000.00 goal for 2025, as of July 13th, 2025, we are at:
25.6% funded
$76,707 donated
Donate to support Django
The next 20 years
20 years is a long time in open source – and we want to keep Django thriving for many more, so it keeps on being the web framework for perfectionists with deadlines as the industry evolves. We don’t know how the web will change it that time, but from Django, you can expect:
Many new releases, each with years of support
Thousands more packages in our
thriving ecosystem
An inclusive and supportive community with hundreds of thousands of developers
Happy 20th birthday, Django!

data.author: nixass
data.article_summary: 这篇文章警告了使用反应性炊具和食物接触可能导致的化学反应问题，特别是“千层面电池”现象。当酸性或含盐的食物（如番茄酱、腌泡汁）与不同金属（如铝箔和钢锅）接触时，可能发生电化学反应，导致铝箔腐蚀、穿孔，甚至产生有毒物质。为避免此问题，建议使用非反应性材料如不锈钢、玻璃、瓷器或搪瓷容器。在烧烤中使用“德州纸巾法”时，也应注意避免铝箔与钢制器具直接接触，推荐使用但纸、烤纸或塑料袋等材料来防止反应。文章还提到，虽然不锈钢一般不易受腐蚀，但仍需注意不同金属间的电化学反应。
